newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF BARCELONA PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF BARCELONA PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Barcelona players ahead of Sunday's Spanish first division match against Valencia:
Vitor Baia, goalkeeper, age 27. Portuguese international who cost 800 million pesetas ($5.59 million) when he moved from Porto last summer. Has come unstuck recently after starting the season well.

Carlos Busquets, goalkeeper, age 29. Nearly ever-present last season, Busquets blew his only chance to prove himself since the arrival of Baia. Heavily-criticised for not using his hands enough, he is often compared to a handball keeper.

Albert Ferrer, defender, 26. Right-sided defender who has reappeared since injury cut short his Euro 96 plans at the end of last season. Ferrer makes up for a lack of physical presence with a terrier-like determination on the wing.
Fernando Couto, defender, 27. Portuguese international has had to sit out several games because of competition for places in the Barcelona defence.
Laurent Blanc, defender, 31. French international, one of Johan Cruyff's last signings, has become a regular in the centre of the defence after initially struggling to impress coach Bobby Robson.
Sergi Barjuan, defender, 24. A key factor down the left in both defence and attack, Sergi is one of the quickest men in the Spanish game and an instant first choice.
Miguel Angel Nadal, defender/midfielder, 30. Surprisingly skillful for a big man, Nadal's failure to hold down a regular place has seen him linked to English champions Manchester United.

Josep Guardiola, midfielder, 26. Classy and intelligent, the playmaker of Spain's 1992 Olympic gold medal side has returned to favour under Robson after being sidelined by Cruyff. Now a regular in the Spain team.

Ivan de la Pena, midfielder, 20. The shaven-headed darling of the Camp Nou crowd is a superb passer and set-piece man. Despite his unreliability has come off the substitutes' bench to take over from Giovanni in recent games.
Guillermo Amor, midfielder, 29. Came good at end of last season with a series of crucial goals which earned him a Euro 96 slot, but has hardly played under Robson.
Roger Garcia, midfielder, 20. Former reserve team player who has been left on the sidelines since the arrival of Robson.

Giovanni, midfielder/striker, 25. Traded Pele's number 10 shirt at Santos for the playmaker role at Barcelona. A fine finisher and a particularly good header of the ball, Giovanni has recently fallen from favour and clashed with coach Robson.
Luis Figo, striker, 24. Skillful Portuguese international who is at home down either the left or right wing. Has been linked to AC Milan recently.

Ronaldo, striker, 20. A series of sensational individual goals made the Brazilian the undisputed king of the Spanish game. He has already gone a long way to justifying the $20 million paid to PSV Eindhoven in the close season. Current World Footballer of the Year.

Juan Pizzi, striker 28. A naturalized Argentine who was Spain's top goalscorer while at Tenerife last season, Pizzi has been left in the shadow of Ronaldo since joining Barcelona. Scores a lot of goals in the limited time he plays.
Hristo Stoichkov, striker, 31. Fiery Bulgarian who has struggled to find a regular place since returning to the Camp Nou from Parma in the close season. An alternative down the left for Amunike.
Emmanuel Amunike, striker, 26. Nigerian winger signed at Robson's request from Sporting Lisbon in the New Year. His poor form has made him the focus for attacks against the coach.
